source_text:
390 ἔζησεν ἕτερα ρν ʹ· τῶν γὰρ τῆς προτέρας εὐημερίας οηʹ ἐτῶν τυγχανόντων, ὁ
διπλοῦς χρόνος τῆς ὕστερον εὐπραγίας ρν ʹ ἔτη συ νάγει· προτιθεμένων δὲ καὶ τῶν
ιδʹ ἐτῶν τῆς πληγῆς, συνάγονται ἔτη ροʹ, καὶ οὕτως εὑρίσκεται ζήσας, μετὰ τὴν
πληγὴν, του τέστιν ἀφ' οὗ ἡ πληγὴ ἐνήνεκται, ἔτη ροʹ κατὰ τὴν γραφήν. Σώζεται δὲ
οὕτω καὶ ἡ διπλασίων τῆς εὐθηνίας ἀνταπόδοσις. Συ νελὼν τοίνυν, ἀριθμήσεις
οὕτως· ἔζησεν ἐν πλούτῳ καὶ εὐπαιδίᾳ ἔτη οηʹ· ἐν τῇ πάν των ἀποβολῇ καὶ τῇ κακίᾳ
τοῦ σώματος ἔτη ιδʹ· ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ εὐπραγίᾳ ἔτη ρνζʹ, ὡς εἶναι τὸν πάντα τῆς ζωῆς
αὐτοῦ χρό νον, ἔτη σμηʹ, καθά φησιν ἡ κατ' αὐτὸν ἱερὰ βίβλος. ιζʹ. Καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν
Ἰὼβ πρεσβύτερος καὶ πληρὴς ἡμερῶν. Γέγραπται δὲ, αὐτὸν πάλιν ἀναστήσεσθαι μεθ'
ὧν ὁ Κύριος ἀνί στησιν. Ἀκύλας καὶ Σύμμαχος ἐλθόντες συνεπέ ραναν τὸ βιβλίον,
ὡς δὴ τῷ ἑβραϊκῷ ἀκο λουθοῦντες· ὁ δὲ Θεοδοτίων συμπεραίνει τοῖς Οʹ, οὐδὲν ἔχων
ἐλλεῖπον, οὐ χρόνον, οὐ βίον. Γέγραπται δὲ πάλιν ἀναστήσεσθαι αὐτὸν, μεθ' ὧν ὁ
Κύριος ἀνίστησιν, τῶν δικαίων δηλονότι· οἱ γὰρ ἀσεβεῖς, φησὶν, οὐκ ἀναστήσονται
ἐν κρίσει, οὐδὲ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐν βουλῇ δικαίων. Καὶ ταῦτα δὲ ῥήματα δεχόμεθα, εἰ
καὶ μὴ ὡς τοῦ παντὸς ὕφους ὄντα, ἀλλά γε ὥς τινος τῶν ἁγίων αὐτὰ συνυφήναντος
τῇ βίβλῳ· πλὴν ὅμως πάντα δεχόμεθα, οὕτως ἐκ τῶν πατέρων τὸ βιβλίον
παρειληφότες. ιηʹ. Οὗτος ἑρμηνεύεται ἐκ τῆς συριακῆς βίβλου. Συριακὴν νῦν τὴν
Ἑβραίων διάλεκτον κα 391 λεῖ, ἐπειδὴ καὶ Συρίαν τὴν Ἰουδαῖαν, καὶ Σύρους οἱ
πολλοὶ τοὺς Παλαιστινοὺς ὀνομάζουσιν· καὶ Ἡρόδοτος ὁ ἱστοριογράφος φησί·
Περιτέμνονται δὲ Ἰνδοὶ, καὶ Αἰγύπτιοι, καὶ Ἄραβες, καὶ οἱ ἐν Παλαιστίνῃ Σύροι· τοὺς
Ἰουδαίους οὕτω καλοῦσιν.
pass_a_gloss: … he lived another 156 (printed 'ρν ʹ'); for the years of the earlier prosperity being 78, the double time of the later good fortune brings together 156 years; and the 14 years of the stroke being set before as well, 170 years are brought together, and so he is found having lived, after the stroke, that is from when the stroke was brought on, 170 years according to the Scripture. And so also the double repayment of the plenty is preserved. Having summed up then, you will count thus: he lived in wealth and good children 78 years; in the casting away of all things and the badness of the body 14 years; in the second good fortune 156 years (printed ρνζʹ, 157), so that the whole time of his life is 248 years, as the holy book concerning him says. Label: verse 17. And Job died, old and full of days. And it is written, he will rise again with whom the Lord raises. Aquila and Symmachus, having come [here], concluded the book, as following the Hebrew; but Theodotion concludes together with the Seventy (Οʹ), having nothing lacking, not time, not life. And it is written that he will rise again, with whom the Lord raises, of the righteous plainly; for the impious, he says, will not rise in judgement, nor the sinners in the council of the righteous. And these words also we receive, even if not as being of the whole web, but at least as of one of the saints having woven them together into the book; but nevertheless we receive all, having thus received the book from the fathers. Label: verse 18. This one is interpreted from the Syrian book. Syrian now he calls the dialect of the Hebrews, since also Judaea [they call] Syria, and the many name the Palestinians Syrians; and Herodotus the history-writer says: Indians are circumcised, and Egyptians, and Arabs, and the Syrians in Palestine; the Jews they call so.
pass_b_english: … he lived another hundred and fifty-six years. For since the years of his former prosperity were seventy-eight, the double time of his later good fortune comes to a hundred and fifty-six years; and when the fourteen years of the stroke are added before them, the total is a hundred and seventy years. So he is found to have lived a hundred and seventy years after the stroke, that is, from the time the stroke was brought on him, as Scripture says. In this way the double repayment of his plenty is also kept. To sum up, then, you will count like this: he lived in wealth and in the blessing of children seventy-eight years; in the loss of everything and the affliction of his body, fourteen years; in his second good fortune, a hundred and fifty-six years; so that the whole time of his life is two hundred and forty-eight years, as the sacred book about him says.

“And Job died, old and full of days” (Job 42:17). “And it is written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord raises up.” Aquila and Symmachus, on reaching this point, ended the book, since they follow the Hebrew; but Theodotion ends it together with the Seventy, leaving nothing out, neither the time nor the life. It is written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord raises up: the righteous, clearly. For “the ungodly,” it says, “will not rise in judgement, nor sinners in the council of the righteous” (Psalm 1:5). We accept these words too, even if not as belonging to the whole fabric of the book, yet as if one of the saints had woven them into it; still, we accept all of it, since we have received the book in this form from the fathers.

“This one is translated from the Syriac book.” Here he calls the language of the Hebrews Syriac, since most people also call Judea Syria and call the Palestinians Syrians. Herodotus the historian, too, says: “The Indians, the Egyptians, the Arabs and the Syrians in Palestine are circumcised”; it is the Jews that they call by this name.

choices.issue: Figures dropped in the old English
choices.choice: Every '[numbers]' replaced by the figure in the Greek: ρνϛʹ 156, οηʹ 78, ιδʹ 14, ροʹ 170, σμηʹ 248.
'ρν ʹ' (twice) read as ρνϛʹ = 156; the stigma was lost. ρνζʹ (157) in the summary read as ρνϛʹ (156): ϛ misread as ζ, since 78 + 14 + 156 = 248 and 78 x 2 = 156. Recorded, not silent.

Ἀκύλας καὶ Σύμμαχος ἐλθόντες συνεπέραναν τὸ βιβλίον: 'on reaching this point, ended the book' (they stop at 'full of days'); Θεοδοτίων συμπεραίνει τοῖς Οʹ: 'ends it together with the Seventy'. Old 'having come together, read the book' and 'concludes the [numbers]' were wrong.

The resurrection line and 'This one is translated from the Syriac book' (label ιηʹ) are LXX additions; quoted without a KJV reference. οὗτος is masculine (the man, Job, or his account); kept as 'This one'.
οἱ ἀσεβεῖς οὐκ ἀναστήσονται ἐν κρίσει, οὐδὲ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐν βουλῇ δικαίων = LXX Psalm 1:5; 'rise' keeps the Greek verb that carries the argument (KJV 'stand').
Συρίαν τὴν Ἰουδαῖαν, καὶ Σύρους οἱ πολλοὶ τοὺς Παλαιστινοὺς ὀνομάζουσιν: most people call Judea Syria and the Palestinians Syrians. Old English reversed it.
Translated as the catena gives it. Herodotus 2.104 (from memory, not checked against a text on disk) names different peoples; no correction made in the reading text.
